title: Graceful deathwatch SLO guardian and circuit escrow
author: Eve Chen
release_notes: Introduce an SLO guardian that provides a conservative, time-bounded SLO credit buffer and a local circuit escrow that preserves in-flight KV state during transient region flaps. Ships behind config flags and a staggered rollout.
description: Context: Multiple incidents over the past quarter showed oscillating regional circuits causing noisy tenant failovers and repeated short-lived SLO violations when probes briefly flapped. This PR introduces a conservative SLO guardian (deathwatch) that smooths short spikes via a small local credit budget and a circuit escrow that snapshots circuit state for fast safe reattachment. Goal: reduce noisy reopen/reclose cycles, prevent cascading evictions, and give operators a lightweight, observable safety net during regional instability. Design summary: 1) SLO guardian maintains a per-tenant short-term credit bucket (configurable window, default 30s, default credits 3) that allows limited headroom for transient latency without immediately triggering global evictions. 2) Circuit escrow persists a minimal circuit snapshot (circuit id, last healthy timestamp, kv-pressure flag) to ephemeral storage on node when a circuit transitions to OPEN; a stale-open timeout and reconciliation loop avoid resurrecting outdated state. 3) Reopen protocol uses escrowed metadata plus a fast-smoothed probe sequence (exponential backoff with capped jitter) to prevent flapping. 4) Telemetry: new metrics (slo_guard_credit_used, slo_guard_trips, escrow_snapshot_count, escrow_reattach_success, escrow_stale_evictions) and traces on reopen paths to diagnose behavior. Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature gated by runtime config (reliability.deathwatch.enabled=false by default), gated rollout to 10% of nodes in canary, and a cluster-level kill switch. Testing and validation: unit tests for bucket accounting and escrow serialization; integration test harness simulating regional probe flaps (added to perf-canary), and a short dogfood run on staging with synthetic spike replay. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of credit bucket and accounting - [x] Circuit escrow snapshot + reconcilers - [x] Metrics + traces + console dashboard stub - [x] Config flags and kill switch - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Runbook update and rollout plan Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary 10% (monitor slo_guard_trips, error_rate, eviction_rate) 2) If stable for 24h, increase to 50% and run a scripted storm test 3) Full rollout with gradual ramping and operator on-call monitoring. Related work: ENG-1298 (regional circuit stability), ENG-1307 (kv-pressure reconciliation), SUP-5412 (incident postmortem). Risks and mitigations: risk of overly permissive credit causing real SLO breaches masked as transient; mitigated via conservative default credits and alerting on credit exhaustion. Also risk of stale escrow reattaching an unhealthy circuit; mitigated by last-healthy-window and reconciliation TTL. Ops notes: added runbook section under docs/operational/deathwatch.md describing how to adjust window/credits and emergency disable. If experimentation shows too many soft-failures, revert by disabling reliability.deathwatch.enabled or scaling down canary. This description is intentionally compact; see changed files for code and docs and review thread for discussion.

review_comments: Marcus Holt: High level - is the credit bucket per-tenant or per-route? If per-tenant we should ensure memory bounds. Also we need a guard against credit starvation during sustained moderate load.

Author (Eve Chen): The default is per-tenant; we add a soft LRU and a max tracked-tenants config (defaults to 50k) to bound memory. Added comments in guardian.go and config/defaults.go to clarify. For starvation, credits are intentionally small and decay; sustained load will exhaust credits and trigger the normal eviction path, with alerts firing.
Priya Shah: Please ensure the escrow snapshots are compact and do not block normal shutdown paths. Also add an integration scenario where the region/controller reboots during reattach.

Author (Eve Chen): Escrow uses a compact binary encoding (proto v1) and writes to ephemeral disk with fsync off by default; added unit test for node shutdown path and added crash-restart scenario to the integration harness.
Diego Alvarez: Telemetry looks good. Request adding a tag to metrics to indicate whether a reopen was caused by guardian credit vs operator action for easier dashboards.
Author (Eve Chen): Added reopen_cause tag with values (manual, credit_reclaim, normal_probe) on escrow_reattach_success and slo_guard_trips metrics.
Marcus Holt: Approved after code comments addressed and canary plan added. Left one nit on a log message phrasing (fixed).
